example: To be honest with you, I'm not really into horror movies.
exampleZh: 坦白讲，我不太喜欢恐怖片。
tip: 放在句首，给自己 1 秒组织后半句。口语里常缩成 To be honest / Honestly。

example: That reminds me of the time I got lost in Tokyo.
exampleZh: 这让我想起有一次我在东京迷路了。
tip: 接别人的话、顺势讲自己故事的万能桥。

example: He's, how should I put it... a bit intense.
exampleZh: 他这个人，怎么说呢……有点用力过猛。
tip: 想不到合适的词时直接说出来，外国人也天天这么用。

example: It's not bad, it's just not my thing, you know what I mean?
exampleZh: 不是不好，只是不是我的菜，你懂我意思吧？
tip: 句尾用，语调上扬。快读接近 Y'know what I mean?

example: Let me think... yeah, Friday works for me.
tip: 被问住时不要沉默，先说这句。

example: It was fine. I mean, the food was great, but the service was slow.
exampleZh: 还行吧。我是说，菜很好吃，但上菜很慢。
tip: 用来补充或修正自己刚说的话。

example: I'm kind of tired, to be honest.
tip: kind of 快读成 kinda，sort of 快读成 sorta。

example: I'd love to come. The thing is, I have work early tomorrow.
exampleZh: 我很想去。问题是我明天一早要上班。
tip: 委婉拒绝或说出真正原因前的铺垫。

example: Anyway, enough about me. How was your weekend?
exampleZh: 好了，不说我了。你周末过得怎么样？
tip: 把跑偏的话题拉回来，或结束自己的话轮。

example: By the way, did you get my message?
exampleZh: 对了，你收到我的消息了吗？
tip: 自然地插入新话题。

example: Actually, I've never been there.
tip: 温和地纠正或给出意外信息。

example: Basically, we just walked around and ate a lot.
exampleZh: 基本上就是到处逛、狂吃。
tip: 把复杂的事一句话概括。

example: It's like... a mix between a cafe and a bookstore.
exampleZh: 它就像……咖啡馆和书店的结合体。
tip: 描述说不清的东西时，用比喻绕过去。

phrase: What I'm trying to say is...
example: What I'm trying to say is, you don't have to do it alone.
exampleZh: 我想说的是，你不必一个人扛。
tip: 说乱了的时候用它重新开始。

example: If you ask me, the first movie was way better.
exampleZh: 要我说，第一部好看多了。
tip: 比 in my opinion 口语得多。

example: Long story short, we missed the flight.
tip: 讲故事时跳到结局，避免自己卡在细节里。

example: Speaking of which, have you tried that new ramen place?
exampleZh: 说到这个，你去过那家新开的拉面店吗？
tip: 顺着对方的话题延伸。

example: Now that you mention it, he did seem a bit off today.
exampleZh: 你这么一说，他今天确实有点怪。
tip: 表示被对方提醒，让对方感觉被认真听了。

example: You'd rather stay in tonight? Fair enough.
exampleZh: 你今晚想待在家？行吧，可以理解。
tip: 接受对方观点，即使不完全同意。

example: I guess we could just order pizza.
exampleZh: 要不我们就点个披萨吧。
tip: 让语气变软，不那么武断。

example: Come to think of it, I haven't seen her in ages.
exampleZh: 仔细想想，我好久没见她了。
tip: 边说边想时的自然开头。

example: Sorry, where was I? Oh right, the party.
exampleZh: 抱歉，我刚说到哪了？哦对，那个派对。
tip: 被打断后接回话题，一点也不尴尬。

example: It's that thing you use to, what's the word, open cans.
exampleZh: 就是那个用来……叫什么来着……开罐头的东西。
tip: 忘词时说出来，对方往往会帮你补上。

example: The store closes at nine, right?
tip: 句尾加 right? 把陈述句变成邀请对方接话。

example: I got up late again this morning.
tip: wake up 是醒来，get up 是从床上起来。

example: I'm gonna sleep in this Saturday.
We ran out of milk. Can you grab some on the way home?
exampleZh: 牛奶喝完了，你回家路上能顺手买点吗？

example: Let me clean up the kitchen first.
Just throw it out, it's expired.
tip: 也可以说 throw away。

example: Put on a jacket, it's freezing outside.
tip: put on 是穿的动作，wear 是穿着的状态。

example: Please take off your shoes at the door.
tip: 也指飞机起飞。

example: Can you turn off the lights?
tip: 反义 turn on。

example: I'll just warm up some leftovers.
tip: 也指运动前热身。

example: I dozed off on the couch watching TV.
exampleZh: 我看电视的时候在沙发上睡着了。

example: I can't figure out how this thing works.
exampleZh: 我搞不懂这玩意儿怎么用。
tip: 口语里出现频率极高。

example: Can you pick up the package from the front desk?
exampleZh: 你能去前台把快递取一下吗？
tip: 也指开车接人：I'll pick you up at seven.

example: Let's put off the meeting till Friday.
tip: put off doing sth = 拖着不做某事。

example: We need to come up with a better plan.
exampleZh: 我们得想个更好的方案。

example: I'll deal with it tomorrow.
I'll look into it and get back to you.
Let me check and get back to you.
I need to catch up on some sleep this weekend.
tip: catch up on emails / work / a show 都常用。

example: Can you fill in for me on Monday?
exampleZh: 周一你能替我顶一下班吗？

example: Sorry for interrupting. Carry on.
Don't give up just yet.
Let's go over the plan one more time.
I'll set up a call for next week.
exampleZh: 我来约个下周的电话会。
tip: 也指安装设备：set up the printer。

example: They called off the game because of the rain.
I still haven't handed in my report.
I'm totally burned out this week.
tip: 名词 burnout = 职业倦怠。

example: I ran into my old roommate at the mall.
exampleZh: 我在商场碰见了以前的室友。

example: Wanna hang out this weekend?
We should grab coffee and catch up sometime.
exampleZh: 找时间喝杯咖啡聊聊近况吧。

example: He said he'd come, but he never showed up.
exampleZh: 他说会来，结果根本没出现。

example: Feel free to drop by anytime.
tip: 也可说 stop by。

example: I get along really well with my coworkers.
They had a fight but made up the next day.
exampleZh: 他们吵了一架，第二天就和好了。
tip: make up a story = 编故事。

example: He finally asked her out.
I don't wanna let you down.
I'm really looking forward to the trip.
tip: to 后面接名词或 doing。

example: You can always count on me.
I had to turn down the invite.
exampleZh: 我只好推掉了这个邀请。
tip: 也指调小音量。

example: We're having some friends over tonight.
exampleZh: 今晚我们请了几个朋友来家里。

example: Can you drop me off at the station?
tip: 反义 pick up（去接）。

example: We need to get off at the next stop.
tip: 上车 get on（公交地铁）/ get in（小汽车）。

example: We set off early to beat the traffic.
exampleZh: 我们早早出发避开堵车。

example: It's easy to get around by subway here.
exampleZh: 这里坐地铁出行很方便。

example: Can you pull over here? I'll get out.
exampleZh: 能在这里靠边停一下吗？我下车。

example: I'm just looking around, thanks.
tip: 店员问 Can I help you? 时的标准回答。

example: Can I try this on?
tip: 代词放中间：try it on。

example: The tickets sold out in minutes.
tip: sold out = 售罄。

example: We lined up for an hour to get in.
exampleZh: 我们排了一个小时队才进去。

example: You should shop around before buying a phone.
exampleZh: 买手机前应该货比三家。

example: You gotta check out this little cafe.
exampleZh: 你一定要去看看这家小咖啡馆。
tip: 在酒店是退房，在超市是结账。

example: I can't put up with the noise anymore.
exampleZh: 我再也忍不了这噪音了。

example: Calm down, it's not a big deal.
tip: 对正在生气的人说可能火上浇油，慎用。

example: Cheer up! It's Friday.
I totally freaked out when I lost my phone.
exampleZh: 手机丢了的时候我整个人都慌了。

example: It took me a while to get over the breakup.
exampleZh: 我花了一段时间才走出那次分手。
tip: Get over it! = 别纠结了！

example: Just chill out, we've got plenty of time.
exampleZh: 放轻松，我们时间多的是。

example: Don't stress out about it.
tip: I'm stressed out. = 我压力好大。

example: You really missed out last night.
tip: FOMO = fear of missing out。

example: We ended up staying home all day.
exampleZh: 结果我们在家待了一整天。
tip: end up doing sth，讲故事结局必备。

example: I totally messed up the presentation.
It turned out to be a great day.
tip: It turns out (that)... = 原来……

example: Don't worry, it'll all work out.
exampleZh: 别担心，一切都会好起来的。
tip: I work out three times a week. = 我一周健身三次。

example: Can you look after my cat this weekend?
exampleZh: 这周末你能帮我照看一下猫吗？

example: I just found out she's moving to Canada.
exampleZh: 我刚知道她要搬去加拿大了。
tip: 闲聊里讲新消息的高频开头。

example: She's going through a tough time right now.
exampleZh: 她最近正经历一段难熬的日子。

example: I didn't wanna bring it up at dinner.
exampleZh: 我不想在饭桌上提这事。

example: Sorry, go on. What happened next?
tip: 鼓励对方继续讲，接话神器。

example: Hold on, let me grab a pen.
tip: hang on 意思一样。

example: Oh, come on, it's not that bad!
tip: 语气不同意思不同，多听原声。

example: Oh sorry, you go ahead.
tip: 两人同时开口时用。

example: Sorry, could you speak up a bit?
exampleZh: 不好意思，能大声一点吗？

example: Sorry to cut in, but I have a quick question.
exampleZh: 抱歉插一句，我有个小问题。

example: What are you getting at?
I couldn't make out what he was saying.
I always mix up their names.
exampleZh: 我老是把他们的名字搞混。

example: He comes across as a bit shy.
I wouldn't rule it out.
So, to sum up, it was a disaster.
exampleZh: 所以总结一下，简直是灾难。

example: Okay, I take it back.
tip: 在商店是退货：take it back to the store。

example: I just blurted it out without thinking.
exampleZh: 我想都没想就脱口而出了。

example: The meeting dragged on for hours.
exampleZh: 那个会拖了好几个小时。

example: We only touched on it briefly.
exampleZh: 我们只是简单提了一下。

example: I think I'll go with the blue one.
tip: 点餐、做选择时超常用。

example: I just went along with it.
I woke up at five and couldn't fall back asleep.
exampleZh: 我五点就醒了，然后再也睡不着。

example: I stayed up way too late last night.
I need to lie down for a bit.
Give me ten minutes to get ready.
Do we need to dress up for this?
Let me wash up before dinner.
Can you put your stuff away?
exampleZh: 你能把你的东西收起来吗？

example: Are you going out tonight?
I think I'll just stay in tonight.
I'll come back later.
I'm looking for my keys.
We just moved in last week.
tip: 反义 move out。

example: Have you settled in yet?
Don't forget to lock up when you leave.
My car broke down on the highway.
exampleZh: 我的车在高速上抛锚了。
tip: She broke down in tears. = 她崩溃大哭。

example: Is the charger plugged in?
Can you turn up the volume?
tip: 也指出现：He didn't turn up.

example: These shoes are falling apart.
I'll give it back tomorrow.
Did I leave anyone out?
Let's eat out tonight.
Wanna grab a bite after work?
exampleZh: 下班后要不要随便吃点？
tip: grab a coffee 同理。

example: I'm too tired to cook, let's just order in.
exampleZh: 我太累了不想做饭，叫外卖吧。
tip: 也可以说 get takeout。

example: We totally pigged out at the buffet.
I'm trying to cut down on sugar.
tip: cut back on 意思接近。

example: Don't fill up on bread.
tip: 加油：fill up the tank。

example: Dinner's ready, dig in!
Eat up, there's plenty more.
Do you wanna split the bill?
I just threw together some pasta.
Get on the number 5 bus.
tip: 小汽车用 get in / get out。

example: Hurry up, we're gonna miss the train!
exampleZh: 快点，我们要赶不上火车了！

example: Slow down, you're driving too fast.
We need to turn around, we missed the exit.
exampleZh: 我们得掉头，错过出口了。

example: Sorry, I'm running a bit late.
tip: 迟到前发消息的标准说法。

example: We got lost on the way there.
tip: 单说 Get lost! 是“滚开”，注意语气。

example: It's getting late, we should head back.
Do you wanna come along?
Hey, wait up!
Sorry, I got held up at work.
tip: What's the holdup? = 怎么卡住了？

example: We can check in after 3 p.m.
exampleZh: 我们下午三点后可以入住。

example: Help me pick out a gift for my mom.
exampleZh: 帮我挑个给我妈的礼物。

example: Twenty bucks for a coffee? What a rip-off!
exampleZh: 一杯咖啡二十刀？太坑了！

example: We should stock up on water.
I'll pay you back next week.
All that practice really paid off.
I'm saving up for a new laptop.
We splashed out on a fancy dinner.
Let's all chip in for her gift.
exampleZh: 我们一起凑钱给她买礼物吧。

example: I need to top up my phone.
I had to cough up fifty bucks for the ticket.
exampleZh: 我不得不掏了五十块买票。

example: I'm still working on it.
Don't worry, we'll sort it out.
I'll follow up with an email.
Thanks for pointing that out.
Can you take over for a minute?
I just need to get through this week.
tip: 打通电话也用：I couldn't get through.

example: I've fallen behind on my work.
It's hard to keep up with everything.
Let me run it by my boss first.
Something came up, I can't make it.
exampleZh: 突然有点事，我去不了了。
tip: 临时爽约的万能理由。

example: I signed up for a yoga class.
Just fill out this form.
Let me look it up.
I need to brush up on my English.
Let's get on with it.
Let's wrap up for today.
The event kicks off at seven.
I slacked off a bit this week.
I'll put together a list.
Let me think it over.
He got laid off last month.
He backed out at the last minute.
We should get together sometime.
Where should we meet up?
Wanna come over for dinner?
They broke up after five years.
exampleZh: 他们在一起五年后分手了。

example: Is he going out with anyone?
We really hit it off.
We fell out over something stupid.
exampleZh: 我们因为点蠢事闹翻了。

example: It took him a while to open up.
exampleZh: 他过了好一阵才敞开心扉。

example: I've always looked up to my older sister.
I can't believe she stood me up.
exampleZh: 真不敢相信她放我鸽子。
tip: bail on sb 也是放鸽子。

example: Mind if I tag along?
He's always showing off his car.
Stop putting yourself down.
She talked me into going.
tip: 反义 talk sb out of。

example: I didn't really fit in at first.
exampleZh: 一开始我不太融得进去。
tip: 日程里：I can fit you in at 3.

example: I'd love to get to know you better.
Thanks for sticking up for me.
Stop picking on your brother.
Back off, I can handle it.
She hung up on me!
I'm fed up with this weather.
I'm completely worn out.
That video cracked me up.
Lighten up, it's just a joke.
I just need some time to cool off.
exampleZh: 我需要点时间冷静一下。

example: Don't take it out on me.
Don't bottle up your feelings.
Don't let it get to you.
You need to let go of the past.
Sorry, I got a bit carried away.
I'm so pumped up for the concert!
Look on the bright side, at least nobody got hurt.
exampleZh: 往好处想，至少没人受伤。

example: I don't feel up to going out tonight.
I think I'm coming down with a cold.
I felt like I was gonna throw up.
He passed out from the heat.
I'm trying to fight off a cold.
exampleZh: 我在扛着不让自己感冒。

example: Don't worry, he'll pull through.
I've put on a bit of weight.
His grandpa passed away last year.
tip: 比 die 委婉。

example: My back is acting up again.
I'm just calling to check up on you.
exampleZh: 我就是打电话问问你怎么样。

example: Don't hang up, I'm still here.
Can I call you back later?
exampleZh: 我晚点给你回电话行吗？

example: She never texted me back.
I can't log in to my account.
tip: 退出登录 log out。

example: I was just scrolling through Instagram.
Make sure you back up your photos.
tip: Back me up here. = 帮我说句话。

example: My laptop keeps shutting down.
exampleZh: 我的电脑老是自动关机。

example: My phone froze up again.
Sorry, I totally zoned out.
Turn on your location.
Can we move the meeting up to 2?
exampleZh: 我们能把会提前到两点吗？

example: They pushed the deadline back a week.
exampleZh: 他们把截止日期推后了一周。

example: I'll try to free up some time on Friday.
exampleZh: 我尽量周五腾出点时间。

example: Let's pencil it in for Saturday.
Sorry, I can't make it tonight.
tip: We made it! = 我们赶上了/成功了！

example: Let me sleep on it.
I like to read to wind down before bed.
You need to plan ahead for the holidays.
I'm about to head out.
We're running behind schedule.
Alright, I'm off. See you!
No way! You actually met him?
tip: 表示惊讶，不是拒绝。

example: Seriously? That's crazy.
Oh, that makes sense now.
This heat is killing me. Tell me about it.
tip: 不是让对方讲，而是表示“我太懂了”。

example: That movie was so good. I know, right?
exampleZh: 那部电影太好看了。——就是说啊！

example: Good point, I didn't think of that.
Oh, that's too bad. Are you okay?
Seven o'clock? Sounds good.
I'm starving. Same here.
I don't really like coffee. Me neither.
exampleZh: 我不太喜欢咖啡。——我也不。
tip: 否定句后用 Me neither，不用 Me too。

example: Are you tired? Not really.
tip: 比直接说 No 柔和。

example: Really? I had no idea.
Exactly! That's what I've been saying.
exampleZh: 没错！我一直就是这么说的。

example: Ah, I see. That's why she left.
exampleZh: 哦，我明白了，难怪她走了。

example: You got the job? Good for you!
exampleZh: 你拿到那份工作了？真为你高兴！

example: You lost your wallet? That sucks.
tip: 熟人之间用，比较随意。

phrase: Sorry, could you say that again?
example: Sorry, could you say that again? It's a bit loud in here.
exampleZh: 抱歉，能再说一遍吗？这里有点吵。
tip: 没听懂时最重要的一句，别装懂。

example: What do you mean by that?
Sorry, I didn't catch your name.
exampleZh: 抱歉，我没听清你的名字。

example: So you're saying we should wait?
exampleZh: 所以你是说我们应该等等？
tip: 复述确认，也给自己争取时间。

phrase: How do you say ... in English?
example: How do you say hotpot in English?
tip: 卡词时直接问，外国人很乐意教。

phrase: Could you speak a bit slower?
example: Sorry, could you speak a bit slower?
Well... it's complicated.
It's, you know, one of those days.
exampleZh: 就是，你知道的，那种倒霉日子。

phrase: Let me put it this way...
example: Let me put it this way, I'm not going back.
exampleZh: 这么说吧，我不会再去了。

example: Hmm, that's a good question.
tip: 被问住时先接这句，争取几秒。

example: I'm not sure, but I think it's on the left.
exampleZh: 我不太确定，不过应该在左边。

example: To be fair, he did say sorry.
exampleZh: 说句公道话，他确实道歉了。

example: Don't get me wrong, I like him, but he talks too much.
exampleZh: 别误会，我挺喜欢他的，但他话太多了。

example: In other words, we're broke.
As far as I know, it's free.
It depends on the weather.
The funny thing is, I'd never even been there.
exampleZh: 好笑的是，我根本没去过那儿。

example: Believe it or not, I've never had pizza.
exampleZh: 信不信由你，我从没吃过披萨。

example: I'm from Shanghai. How about you?

example: Out of curiosity, how did you two meet?
exampleZh: 好奇问一下，你俩是怎么认识的？

example: Funny you should say that, I was just thinking about it.
exampleZh: 说来也巧，我刚还在想这事。

example: Oh, before I forget, here's your book.
exampleZh: 哦，趁我还没忘，这是你的书。

meaning: 最近怎么样？有啥新鲜事？
example: Hey! So, what's new with you?
tip: 闲聊开场白。

example: Hey! How's it going?
tip: 最常用的打招呼，回答 Pretty good, you? 即可。

example: Hey, long time! How have you been?
exampleZh: 嘿，好久不见！你最近还好吗？

example: Long time no see! You look great.

phrase: What have you been up to?
example: So, what have you been up to lately?
Morning! How was your weekend?
tip: 周一闲聊的标准开场。

example: How's it going? Pretty good, you?
exampleZh: 最近怎么样？——挺好的，你呢？
tip: 回答完马上反问，不冷场。

example: You went surfing? That sounds fun!
exampleZh: 你去冲浪了？听起来好好玩！

example: You got a new job? Oh, cool!
exampleZh: 你换新工作了？哦，不错啊！

example: You had the interview today? How did it go?
exampleZh: 你今天面试了？结果怎么样？
tip: 对方提到一件事时的万能追问。

example: Wait, what happened next?
tip: Then what? 更口语。

example: You're moving out? How come?
tip: 比 Why? 更随意、更不像质问。

example: You've been to Iceland? What was it like?
exampleZh: 你去过冰岛？感觉怎么样？

phrase: I'd love to hear about it.
example: You went to the concert? I'd love to hear about it.
exampleZh: 你去看演唱会了？我很想听听。

example: Your dog is sick? I'm sorry to hear that.
exampleZh: 你的狗病了？真替你难过。
tip: 不是道歉，是表示同情。

example: Working two jobs? That must be tough.
exampleZh: 打两份工？那一定很难熬。

example: I know it's hard right now. Hang in there.
exampleZh: 我知道现在很难，坚持住。

example: Don't blame yourself, it's not your fault.
Sorry I'm late. Don't worry about it.
exampleZh: 抱歉我迟到了。——没事，别放在心上。

phrase: I'm not so sure about that.
example: Cheaper is always better? I'm not so sure about that.
exampleZh: 便宜的总是更好？我可不太确定。
tip: 比直接说 You're wrong 礼貌得多。

example: I see your point, but I still think it's too expensive.
exampleZh: 我明白你的意思，但我还是觉得太贵了。

phrase: I get what you're saying, but...
example: I get what you're saying, but it's not that simple.
exampleZh: 我懂你的意思，不过没那么简单。

example: He's the best player ever? I don't know about that.
exampleZh: 他是史上最强？这可不好说。

example: Maybe, but we should still ask first.
exampleZh: 也许吧，但我们还是应该先问一下。

example: Guess what? I got the job!
exampleZh: 你猜怎么着？我拿到那份工作了！
tip: 讲好消息前吊胃口。

example: You won't believe this, but I saw a celebrity today.
exampleZh: 你肯定不信，我今天看到明星了。

example: So get this, the restaurant was closed when we got there.
exampleZh: 听我说，我们到的时候餐厅居然关门了。
tip: 讲到精彩处的口语开头。

example: And then the power went out.
All of a sudden, it started pouring.
exampleZh: 突然之间就下起了大雨。

example: It turns out he was joking the whole time.
exampleZh: 结果原来他一直在开玩笑。

example: Oops, my bad. I'll fix it.
tip: 小失误时用，很口语。

example: Thanks for waiting! No worries.
I forgot to call you back, sorry about that.
exampleZh: 我忘了给你回电话，抱歉啊。

example: Thanks for the ride, I appreciate it.
You don't know? Okay, thanks anyway.
exampleZh: 你也不知道？好吧，还是谢谢你。

example: Can you pass the salt? No problem.
exampleZh: 能把盐递给我吗？——没问题。

example: Anyway, I should get going.
tip: 礼貌地结束聊天。

phrase: It was nice talking to you.
example: It was nice talking to you. See you around!
exampleZh: 很高兴和你聊天，回头见！

example: Alright, catch you later!
Let's keep in touch, okay?
Okay, talk to you soon!
You passed the test? That's awesome!
You fixed it already? Good job!
Wow, you look great today.
I love your shirt! Thanks, that's nice of you.
exampleZh: 我喜欢你的衬衫！——谢谢，你真好。
tip: 被夸时的回应，不要说 No no no。

example: Let's grab a coffee or something.
exampleZh: 我们去喝个咖啡什么的吧。
tip: 说不清具体时挂在句尾。

example: We talked about work and stuff like that.
Yeah, that's pretty much it.
I'm more or less done.
Turn left at the light? Got it.
So we meet at six, does that make sense?
exampleZh: 所以我们六点见，这样清楚吗？
tip: 解释完确认对方听懂。

example: I feel like it's gonna rain.
tip: 年轻人口语里 I think 的替代。

example: Personally, I prefer the old version.
I'd say it takes about an hour.
exampleZh: 我觉得大概要一个小时。
tip: 给估计、判断时用。

example: Let me see... I think it was last Tuesday.
Give me a sec, I'm thinking.
How can I explain this... it's like a Chinese pancake.
exampleZh: 这个怎么解释呢……就像一种中式煎饼。
